### Symbols for spacetime and geometry

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x^\mu$, $\mu = 0, 1, 2, 3$ | spacetime coordinates, $x^\mu = (t, \mathbf x)$; Greek indices run over $0, \dots, 3$, Latin $i, j, k$ over $1, 2, 3$ |
| $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \operatorname{diag}(1, -1, -1, -1)$ | Minkowski metric |
| $g_{\mu\nu}$, $g^{\mu\nu}$ | metric and inverse metric |
| $g = \det g_{\mu\nu}$ | determinant of the metric; actions carry $\sqrt{-g}$ |
| $\Lambda^\mu{}_\nu$ | Lorentz transformation, $V^\mu \mapsto \Lambda^\mu{}_\nu V^\nu$ |
| $\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ | d'Alembertian, $\partial_t^2 - \nabla^2$ ($\nabla^\mu\nabla_\mu$ on a curved spacetime) |
| $\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}$ | Levi-Civita symbol, $\epsilon_{0123} = +1$ |
| $\mathbf x$, $\mathbf k$ | position and wave vector in physical space |
| $\mathbf n$ | unit vector |
| $T_pM$, $T^*_pM$ | tangent and cotangent spaces at $p$ |
| $C^\infty(M)$ | smooth functions on a manifold $M$ |
| $\partial_i\vert_p$, $dx^i\vert_p$ | coordinate basis of $T_pM$ and its dual basis, the coordinate differentials |
| $\dot\gamma(t)$ | velocity of a curve $\gamma$, a tangent vector at $\gamma(t)$ |
| $dF_p$, $F_*X$ | differential (pushforward) of a smooth map at $p$; pushforward of a vector field by a diffeomorphism |
| $F^*T$ | pullback of a covariant tensor field or form by a smooth map $F$; for a diffeomorphism also of vector fields and mixed tensors, $F^*Y = (F^{-1})_*Y$ |
| $[X, Y]$ | Lie bracket of vector fields, $[X, Y](f) = X(Y(f)) - Y(X(f))$ |
| $\Omega^k(M)$, $dx^I$ | $k$-forms on $M$; $dx^{i_1} \wedge \dots \wedge dx^{i_k}$ for $i_1 < \dots < i_k$ |
| $\operatorname{rank}_pF$ | rank of a smooth map $F$ at $p$ |
| $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $\partial\mathbb{R}^n_+$ | closed half-space $\{\mathbf a : a^n \geq 0\}$ and its boundary $\{a^n = 0\}$ |
| $\partial M$, $\operatorname{Int}M$ | boundary and interior of a manifold with boundary |
| $\operatorname{supp}f$ | support of a function or form, the closure of the set where it is non-zero |
| $\int_M\omega$ | integral of a compactly supported top-degree form over an oriented manifold |
| $\mathbf J$, $\mathbf G = \mathbf J^\top\mathbf J$ | Jacobian of a parametrisation and its Gram matrix |
| $O_n$ | the set of $n \times n$ matrices with $\mathbf A^\top\mathbf A = \mathbf I$ |
| $\Phi_t$, $\mathcal D$, $M_t$ | flow of a vector field at time $t$, its flow domain in $\mathbb R \times M$, and the open set of points where $\Phi_t$ is defined |
| $\mathcal L_X$ | Lie derivative along the vector field $X$ (always written with its field) |
| $\iota_X\omega$ | interior product, $\omega(X, \cdot, \dots, \cdot)$ |
| $\operatorname{Kill}(g)$ | vector space of Killing fields of a metric $g$ |
| $D$, $D_p$ | distribution ($k$-plane field) and its plane at $p$; not the distributions (generalised functions) of Fourier analysis |
| $\omega$, $\omega_0$, $\boldsymbol\Omega$ | symplectic form; standard form $\sum_idq^i \wedge dp_i$ of $\mathbb R^{2n}$, $\omega_0(\mathbf u, \mathbf v) = \mathbf u^\top\boldsymbol\Omega\mathbf v$ with $\boldsymbol\Omega = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf 0 & \mathbf I_n \\ -\mathbf I_n & \mathbf 0 \end{pmatrix}$ |
| $\theta = p_i\,dq^i$ | canonical one-form of phase space, $\omega = -d\theta$ |
| $S^\omega$ | symplectic complement of a subspace $S$ |
| $X_H$, $\{f, g\}$ | Hamiltonian vector field, $\iota_{X_H}\omega = dH$; Poisson bracket $\omega(X_f, X_g) = \sum_i(\partial_{q^i}f\,\partial_{p_i}g - \partial_{p_i}f\,\partial_{q^i}g)$ |
| $d$ | exterior derivative |
| $\nabla_XY$, $\Gamma^k_{ij}$ | covariant derivative of $Y$ along $X$ for a connection $\nabla$; its coefficients, $\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j = \Gamma^k_{ij}\partial_k$ |
| $T(X, Y)$, $T^k_{ij}$ | torsion of a connection, $\nabla_XY - \nabla_YX - [X, Y]$ |
| $D_tV$ | covariant derivative of a vector field $V$ along a curve |
| $P_{a \to t}$ | parallel transport along a curve from $\gamma(a)$ to $\gamma(t)$ |
| $\exp_p$ | exponential map at $p$, $\exp_p(v) = \gamma_v(1)$ |
| $R(X, Y)Z$ | Riemann tensor as an operator, $\nabla_X\nabla_YZ - \nabla_Y\nabla_XZ - \nabla_{[X, Y]}Z$ |
| $K(X, Y)$, $K$ | sectional curvature of the plane of $X, Y$; Gauss curvature of a surface |
| $h_{ij}$, $S^i{}_j$, $\kappa_1, \kappa_2$, $H$ | second fundamental form, shape operator, principal and mean curvature of a surface in $\mathbb R^3$ (not the metric perturbation $h_{\mu\nu}$ of gravity) |
| $\star$ | Hodge star, $\alpha \wedge \star\beta = \langle\alpha, \beta\rangle_g\operatorname{vol}_g$ |
| $S^n$ | $n$-sphere |
| $T^n$ | $n$-torus, $n \ge 2$ (the circle is $S^1$; the Sobolev spaces of Fundamentals of Mathematics for Physicists also write $T^1$ for the unit circle) |
| $\mathbb{RP}^n$, $\mathbb{CP}^n$ | real and complex projective spaces |
| $f \simeq g$, $f \simeq g\ \mathrm{rel}\ A$, $X \simeq Y$ | homotopic maps; homotopic keeping $A$ fixed; homotopy equivalent spaces |
| $\gamma \simeq_p \delta$, $[\gamma]$ | path-homotopic paths (ends fixed); path class |
| $\gamma \cdot \delta$, $\bar\gamma$, $c_x$ | concatenation (first $\gamma$, then $\delta$), reverse path $\bar\gamma(s) = \gamma(1 - s)$, constant path at $x$ |
| $\pi_1(X, x_0)$, $f_\#$ | fundamental group of $X$ at $x_0$; homomorphism $[\gamma] \mapsto [f \circ \gamma]$ induced by a continuous map $f$ |
| $p : \tilde X \to X$, $\tilde\gamma$ | covering map; lift of a path $\gamma$ through it |
| $\omega_k$, $\deg f$ | the loop $s \mapsto e^{2\pi iks}$ in $S^1$; degree of a closed curve in $S^1$ or of a map $S^1 \to S^1$, and of a smooth map $F$ of compact connected oriented manifolds of the same dimension, $\int_MF^*\omega = \deg F\int_N\omega$ |
| $I^n$, $\partial I^n$, $\pi_n(X, x_0)$ | unit cube $[0, 1]^n$ and its boundary; $n$-th homotopy group (classes of maps $(I^n, \partial I^n) \to (X, x_0)$), $\pi_0$ the set of path components |
| $f \cdot_i g$ | concatenation of two $n$-loops in the $i$-th coordinate |
| $J_n$, $\partial : \pi_n(B) \to \pi_{n-1}(F)$ | the set $(I^n \times \{0\}) \cup (\partial I^n \times [0, 1])$ on which a lift is prescribed; boundary map of a fibration with fibre $F$ |
| $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$, $[\omega]$, $F^*$ | de Rham cohomology, closed $k$-forms modulo exact ones; class of a closed form; map induced by a smooth $F$ |
| $\operatorname{ind}_pX$, $\chi(M)$ | index of an isolated zero of a vector field; Euler characteristic of a closed oriented surface, the sum of the indices |
| $c_k$, $c_1$, $c(F)$ | Chern classes of a $U(n)$ bundle, from $\det(\mathbf I + \frac i{2\pi}F) = 1 + c_1(F) + c_2(F) + \dots$; first Chern class |
| $e(E)$ | Euler class of an oriented rank-two bundle, $[\frac1{2\pi}F^1{}_2]$; $e(TM) = [\frac1{2\pi}K\,dA]$ for a surface |
| $\operatorname{ch}$, $p_k$, $\hat A$ | Chern character $[\operatorname{tr}\exp(\frac i{2\pi}F)]$; Pontryagin forms, from $\det(\mathbf I + \frac1{2\pi}\Omega)$; the $\hat A$ form $1 - \frac{p_1}{24} + \frac{7p_1^2 - 4p_2}{5760} + \dots$ |
| $\mathbb H^2$ | hyperbolic plane |
| $\mathbb D$ | unit disc, the Poincaré disc with the metric $4(du^2 + dv^2)/(1 - u^2 - v^2)^2$ |
| $\mathbb R^{1, n-1}$, $\eta_{p, q}$ | Minkowski space $\mathbb R^n$ with $\eta = \operatorname{diag}(1, -1, \dots, -1)$; $\operatorname{diag}(1, \dots, 1, -1, \dots, -1)$ with $p$ entries $1$ and $q$ entries $-1$ |
| $ds^2 = g_{ij}\,dx^idx^j$ | line element of a metric, with $dx^idx^j$ the symmetrised product |
| $\lvert X\rvert$, $\angle(X, Y)$ | norm $\sqrt{g(X, X)}$ and angle for a Riemannian metric |
| $X^\flat$, $\omega^\sharp$ | index lowered, $g(X, \cdot)$; index raised with $g^{ij}$ |
| $\operatorname{grad}f$ | gradient $(df)^\sharp$ for a metric (on Euclidean space, $\nabla f$) |
| $\operatorname{div}\mathbf F$, $\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F$ | divergence $\star d\star\mathbf F^\flat = -\delta\mathbf F^\flat$ of a vector field for a metric; curl $(\star d\mathbf F^\flat)^\sharp$ on an oriented Riemannian 3-manifold (on Euclidean space, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$ and $\nabla\times\mathbf F$) |
| $L(\gamma)$ | length of a curve, the proper time for a timelike curve in a Lorentzian metric |
| $\operatorname{vol}_g$, $\operatorname{vol}(M)$ | Riemannian volume form of an oriented manifold, $\sqrt{\lvert\det g\rvert}\,dx^1 \wedge \dots \wedge dx^n$ in a positive chart; volume |
| $\langle\alpha, \beta\rangle_g$ | inner product of $k$-forms, $\tfrac{1}{k!}\alpha_{i_1 \dots i_k}\beta^{i_1 \dots i_k}$ |
| $\delta$ | codifferential, $(-1)^{n(k+1)+1+q}\star d\star$ on $k$-forms ($q$ negative signs in the signature) |
| $\Delta_H$ | Hodge Laplacian $d\delta + \delta d$; on Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$, $-\Delta$ on each component |
| $\pi : E \to M$, $E_p$, $\Phi_U$, $g_{UV}$ | fibre bundle with projection $\pi$; fibre $\pi^{-1}(p)$; local trivialisation $\pi^{-1}(U) \to U \times F$; transition functions, $\Phi_U \circ \Phi_V^{-1}(p, f) = (p, g_{UV}(p)f)$ |
| $P \times_G F$, $P \times_\rho V$, $[p, f]$ | bundle associated with a principal $G$-bundle $P$ and an action on $F$ (a representation $\rho$ on $V$): classes of $(p \cdot g, f) \sim (p, g \cdot f)$ |
| $\omega$, $\Omega$, $X^\sharp$ | on a principal bundle: connection one-form, its curvature $d\omega + \omega \wedge \omega$, and the fundamental field $\frac{d}{dt}p \cdot e^{tX}\vert_{t=0}$ of $X \in \mathfrak g$ |
| $\tau_x$, $\operatorname{Hol}_p(x)$ | parallel transport along a curve $x$ in a principal bundle; holonomy of a loop, $\tau_x(p) = p \cdot \operatorname{Hol}_p(x)$ |

Conventions:

- The metric signature is $(+, -, -, -)$, and $(+, -, \dots, -)$ in higher dimensions, where the internal metric is
  negative definite. Timelike vectors have $\eta(v, v) > 0$. Riemannian metrics are positive definite.
- Indices repeated once up and once down are summed (Einstein convention).
- A formula quoted from a source with the signature $(-, +, +, +)$ is converted with $g_{\mu\nu} \to -g_{\mu\nu}$. This
  leaves $\Gamma$, $R^\rho{}_{\sigma\mu\nu}$, $R_{\mu\nu}$ and $F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ unchanged and flips the signs of
  $R$, of $\Box$, of every contraction with an odd number of inverse metrics, and of the metric in the Clifford
  relation. The source's signature is named whenever its form is shown.
- $\epsilon_{0123} = +1$, so $\epsilon^{0123} = -1$.
